A man in his 40s with a medical history of factor VII deficiency hemophilia presented with acute hypoxic respiratory failure. Following admission, he was intubated with prone positioning, and treatment was initiated. He was also found to have Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia. Three days after admission, the patient developed erythema and edematous necrotic plaques of the bilateral ears. No devices had been used on the ears. The necrosis progressed during the following days, primarily involving the earlobe of the right ear and a large portion of the helix of the left ear.
Erythematous plaque (2 cm) with overlying eschar on the right earlobe. Multiple erythematous edematous erosions with eschar and crust on the helical rim of the left ear.

A 9-year-old Chinese girl presenting with symptoms since birth. The patient has thickened nails, keratinized plaques on palms, soles, and corners of the mouth. At age 1, her fingernails and toenails began to turn yellow and thicken. The skin of stressed parts of palms and soles gradually became keratinized, thickened, black and chapped.
